_rules.criticalSuccess: Natural 10 on the d10: roll another 1d10 and ADD it to the first roll. A second 10 does NOT trigger another Critical Success — crits never chain.
_rules.criticalFailure: Natural 1 on the d10: roll another 1d10 and SUBTRACT it from STAT + Skill + first roll. A second 1 does NOT trigger another Critical Failure — crits never chain.
_rules.modifiers: Modifier Values are subtracted from the roll.
_rules._verified: Exact wording confirmed against p.130. This resolves the previously-flagged open question about crit chaining: it does not chain, in either direction.

difficultyValues.name: Simple
difficultyValues.description: Something most people can do without thinking, but which might be hard for a small child.

difficultyValues.name: Everyday
difficultyValues.description: Something most people can do without a lot of special training.

difficultyValues.name: Difficult
difficultyValues.description: Difficult to accomplish without training or natural talent.

difficultyValues.name: Professional
difficultyValues.description: Takes actual training; the user can be considered a professional, skilled in their abilities.

difficultyValues.name: Heroic
difficultyValues.description: A highly skilled feat; one that only the best of the best can pull off. The level of sports stars and other highly regarded superstars.

difficultyValues.name: Incredible
difficultyValues.description: A tremendous feat. Pulling this off would rate you among the very best of your class professionally. Truly Olympian mettle.

difficultyValues.name: Legendary
difficultyValues.description: An awe-inspiring feat. Something people write stories about; spoken of in hushed tones for years to come.
